questions.stem: What does « Elle est bien dans sa peau » mean?
options: She is wearing a warm coat.
She is easily hurt by others.
She is at ease with herself.
questions.explanation: « Être bien dans sa peau » is an idiom: feeling at ease with yourself. Its opposite, « être mal dans sa peau », often comes up in discussions of adolescence.

questions.stem: Which expression means 'the generation gap'?
questions.explanation: « Un fossé » is a ditch or gap, so « le fossé des générations » is the gap in outlook between age groups. « La génération perdue » is the 'lost generation', a different idea.

questions.stem: What is « le surmenage »?
questions.explanation: « Se surmener » is to overwork yourself, and « le surmenage » is the exhaustion that follows. It is a key word for health and wellbeing and for work–life balance.

questions.stem: Which phrase means 'to lead a healthy life'?
questions.explanation: « Sain » means 'healthy' and « saint » means 'holy', so « une vie sainte » is a saintly life. « Gagner sa vie » means 'to earn a living'.

questions.stem: What does « avoir le cafard » mean?
questions.explanation: « Le cafard » is literally a cockroach, but the idiom means feeling low or homesick. « Avoir de la chance » is 'to be lucky'.

questions.stem: What does « Il a un poil dans la main » say about him?
questions.explanation: The image is a hand so idle that hair grows on the palm. Clumsiness has its own idioms, such as « avoir deux mains gauches ».

questions.stem: Which word completes « Il est sympa, mais un peu ___ : il ne paie jamais sa part. »?
questions.explanation: « Radin » is informal for 'stingy', which is what never paying your share shows. « Généreux » is the opposite, and « bavard » means 'talkative'.

questions.stem: What does « la parité » mean in « La loi impose la parité sur les listes électorales »?
options: Equal pay for the same work
The right of every adult to vote
Equal numbers of women and men
questions.explanation: « La parité » is equal representation of women and men, here on lists of candidates. Equal pay is « l'égalité salariale », a separate issue under gender equality.

questions.stem: What does « Elle a atteint la majorité » mean?
options: She is the eldest in her family.
She has become a senior manager.
She has won most of the votes.
questions.explanation: « La majorité » is the age of legal adulthood, 18 in France, when a person gains rights such as voting. Winning most votes is « obtenir la majorité des voix », with a different verb and object.

questions.stem: Which phrase means 'online bullying'?
questions.explanation: « Harceler » means 'to harass', so « le harcèlement » is bullying or harassment. « La dépendance » means 'addiction', a different online problem.

questions.stem: What does « s'entendre bien avec quelqu'un » mean?
options: To get on well with someone
questions.explanation: « Entendre » alone means 'to hear', but the pronominal « s'entendre avec » means 'to get on with'. Waiting is « attendre », a separate verb.

questions.stem: What does « se réconcilier » mean?
options: To meet someone for the first time
To make up after an argument
questions.explanation: « Se réconcilier » is to make peace again, and it usually follows « se disputer » ('to argue'). Breaking off a relationship is « rompre ».

questions.stem: What does « Elle m'a posé un lapin » mean?
options: She played a trick on me.
She gave me a pet rabbit.
questions.explanation: « Poser un lapin à quelqu'un » means not turning up to a meeting. « Poser une question » is the expression for asking a question.

questions.stem: What is « un animal de compagnie »?
questions.explanation: « La compagnie » is company, so an « animal de compagnie » is kept for companionship. A guide dog is « un chien guide d'aveugle ».

questions.stem: « Mes parents me font confiance, mais ils exigent que je rentre avant minuit. » What does the speaker say?
options: They trust her but set a curfew.
Her parents do not trust her to go out.
She can stay out as late as she likes.
She must be home before midday.
questions.explanation: « Faire confiance à » means 'to trust', and « exiger que » + subjunctive is 'to insist that'. « Minuit » is midnight; midday is « midi ».

questions.stem: What does « une famille d'accueil » mean for an exchange student?
questions.explanation: « L'accueil » is welcome or reception, so a « famille d'accueil » hosts a visitor. A blended family is « une famille recomposée ».

questions.stem: You meet your exchange partner's grandmother for the first time. What do you say?
questions.explanation: An older person you have just met is addressed with « vous » and a title such as « madame ». « Salut » and « coucou » are for friends, and « tu » would be too familiar.

questions.stem: Your friend says « J'ai passé un week-end génial ! ». Which reply keeps the conversation going?
questions.explanation: « Ah bon ? » shows interest and « raconte ! » ('tell me about it') hands the turn back. « Ça m'est égal » ('I don't care') closes the topic down.

questions.stem: In a formal interview, how do you ask someone to repeat a question?
questions.explanation: « Vous » and the conditional « pourriez » make the request polite. « Tu peux répéter ? » is fine with friends, but too familiar for an interview.

questions.stem: Which phrase politely ends a phone call with a teacher?
questions.explanation: Closing politely means thanking the person and using a full « au revoir » with a title such as « madame ». « Salut », « ciao » and « bisous » are for friends, however friendly the rest of the call.

questions.stem: In conversation, what are « euh… », « bon » and « ben » used for?
questions.explanation: These fillers hold your turn while you find the words, as 'um' and 'well' do in English. Using a few sounds natural in a spoken interaction.

questions.stem: Your host asks « Ça te dit de venir au marché avec nous ? ». What is she asking?
options: What did you say at the market with us?
Can you tell us the way to the market?
Would you like to come to the market with us?
Did someone tell you to come to the market?
questions.explanation: « Ça te dit de… ? » is an informal invitation: 'do you feel like…?'. Taking « dire » literally, as in 'tell', is the trap.

questions.stem: A friend says « Je n'en peux plus ! » after a long week. What does she mean?
options: She has none of it left to share.
She is not allowed to go out any more.
She is worn out and can't take any more.
She can no longer find what she lost.
questions.explanation: « Ne plus en pouvoir » means being exhausted or at the end of your patience. 'Having none left' is « je n'en ai plus », with « avoir » instead of « pouvoir ».

questions.stem: How do you greet with « faire la bise »?
options: With a kiss on each cheek
With a wave from a distance
With a bow of the head
questions.explanation: Between friends and family in France, « la bise » is a light kiss on each cheek. The number of kisses varies by region. A handshake is « une poignée de main », more usual in formal settings.

questions.stem: What is « une année sabbatique » for a school leaver?
questions.explanation: « Une année sabbatique » is a year off between school and further study, often used to travel or work. A leap year is « une année bissextile ».

questions.stem: What does « la vie active » mean?
questions.explanation: « Entrer dans la vie active » means starting work. It looks as if it means an active lifestyle, but that is « une vie sportive ».

questions.stem: What is « un petit boulot »?
questions.explanation: « Le boulot » is informal for work, and « un petit boulot » is a casual or part-time job, often done by students. A small business is « une petite entreprise ».

questions.stem: In France, what is « le bac »?
options: An entrance test for primary school
questions.explanation: « Le baccalauréat » is taken at the end of the lycée and gives access to higher education. A bachelor's degree is « une licence ».

questions.stem: What does « Je compte faire une licence de droit » mean?
options: I am counting on a licence to practise law.
I have just finished a law degree.
I am working out the cost of law school.
I intend to do a law degree.
questions.explanation: « Compter » + infinitive means 'to intend to', and « une licence » is a three-year university degree. Reading « licence » as a permit is the false friend.

questions.stem: What does « Je suis en terminale » tell you about a French student?
options: She is in her first year of university.
She is in a vocational course.
She is in her final year of lycée.
She is in her last year of primary school.
questions.explanation: « La terminale » is the last year of the lycée, when students sit the bac. The lycée years run seconde, première, terminale.

questions.stem: What does « les études supérieures » mean?
questions.explanation: « Supérieur » here means 'higher', so these are studies after secondary school, at university or another institution. They are broader than postgraduate research.

questions.stem: Which document goes with « un CV » in a job application?
questions.explanation: « Une lettre de motivation » is a cover letter explaining why you want the position. « Une lettre de démission » is a resignation letter.

questions.stem: What is « un entretien d'embauche »?
questions.explanation: « L'embauche » is hiring, and « un entretien » is an interview, so it is the interview before a job offer. A contract is « un contrat de travail ».

questions.stem: What is « un métier d'avenir »?
options: A job you did in the past
questions.explanation: « L'avenir » is the future, so a « métier d'avenir » is a career with growing demand. A former job is « un ancien métier ».

questions.stem: What is « l'équilibre entre vie professionnelle et vie privée »?
questions.explanation: « L'équilibre » is balance, between working life and private life. It is a standard phrase for a discussion of careers and wellbeing.

questions.stem: What does « J'ai hâte de commencer mes études » mean?
options: I am afraid of starting my studies.
I hate the idea of starting my studies.
I am looking forward to starting my studies.
I am in a great hurry to get my studies over with.
questions.explanation: « Avoir hâte de » means being eager or impatient to do something. « Hâte » looks like English 'hate', but the two words are unrelated.

questions.stem: Which phrase means 'lifelong learning'?
options: la formation tout au long de la vie
la vie active après les études
questions.explanation: « Tout au long de la vie » means 'throughout life', so this is learning that carries on after formal schooling. « La formation initiale » is the opposite: the training you complete before starting work.

questions.stem: What does « postuler à un emploi » mean?
questions.explanation: « Postuler » means 'to apply for', and « une candidature » is the application. Advertising a job yourself is « publier une offre d'emploi ».

questions.stem: Which opening suits an email to a host family you have never met?
questions.explanation: A first contact with adults you do not know takes a formal opening and « vous » throughout. « Salut » and « coucou » assume you already know each other well.

questions.stem: Which closing suits a formal letter applying for a job?
options: Grosses bises de la part de toute la famille.
Allez, je te laisse, j'ai plein de trucs à faire.
Veuillez agréer, Madame, l'expression de mes salutations distinguées.
Je t'embrasse très fort et à bientôt, j'espère.
questions.explanation: French formal letters close with a set phrase such as « veuillez agréer… mes salutations distinguées ». The other three are informal sign-offs for family and friends.

questions.stem: « Ce que j'apprécie le plus chez mon meilleur ami, c'est sa franchise. » What does the writer value most?
questions.explanation: « La franchise » means frankness or honesty. It looks like « français » or English 'franchise', but neither is the meaning here.
